title: Week-of go-live burnbox & SLA escrow playbook for multi-surface releases
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Objective:
Create a deterministic, minimal-latency operational playbook that the launch triangle (PM, Eng, SRE) and regional oncall teams can use during the critical week-of cutover for runtime/console/api coordinated releases. The playbook introduces a 'burnbox' escalation lane (dedicated capacity and a small ops team) and an 'SLA escrow' policy (pre-allocated capacity and automated routing to preserve customer SLAs during unexpected degradation).

Scope:
- Applies to multi-surface launches that change runtime model routing, console feature gating, or API rate limit/quotas.
- Includes runbook steps, ownership roster, automated scripts, rollback criteria, and postmortem gating.
- Excludes ongoing long-running migrations — separate migration playbook will be used.

Key deliverables:
1) Week-of actionable runbook (one-pager + step-by-step checklist)
2) Burnbox configuration templates (capacity reservation, throttles, traffic split, oncall rota)
3) SLA escrow policy doc and automation (route override, quota top-up script)
4) Canary signals and dashboards (latency, p99, error-rate threshold definitions)
5) Communication templates (customer comms, internal ops notifications)

Acceptance criteria:
- Runbook validated in a dry-run with at least two regions and >1 internal customer (DevX and Billing) participating.
- Burnbox automation can be triggered with a single CLI command and reverts safely after 30m.
- SLA escrow triggers re-route without token loss and preserves p95 latency under degraded host counts.
- Stakeholders sign-off: SRE Lead, Runtime Eng Lead, Console PM, Compliance.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Pre-reserving capacity (burnbox) increases short-term cost for launches; offset by limiting burnbox to 6 hours and strict opt-in.
- SLA escrow complexity may mask slow regressions; mitigations: clear observability and mandatory post-launch regressions tests.
- Automation must be fail-safe; manual rollback steps included as fallback.
